source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם שְׁכֶ֑מָה כִּ֥י שְׁכֶ֛ם בָּ֥אוּ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Rehoboam to Shechem, for [to] Shechem had come all Israel to make king him.

en.L: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come [to] Shechem to make him king.
en.B: Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had gathered at Shechem to make him king.
en.R: Rehoboam went to the town of Shechem. All the people of Israel had gathered there to make him their king.

decisions.choice: the same account as 1 Kings 12:1
decisions.reason: Chronicles 10:1-19 retells 1 Kings 12:1-19 almost word for word. In this verse the Hebrew differs only in small points of form: Shechem carries an ending that means "to", and "had come" is plural where Kings has the singular. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Shechem: the old meeting place of the northern tribes
decisions.reason: Shechem lay in the hill country of Ephraim (1 Kings 12:25). Joshua gathered the tribes there to renew the covenant (Joshua 24:1, 25), and Abimelech was made king there (Judges 9:6). Rehoboam goes to the northern tribes; they do not come to him in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: to make him king: to accept him as their king
decisions.reason: Solomon's son already reigned in Jerusalem (9:31), but the tribes of Israel still had to accept him. The elders of Israel had made a covenant with David before they anointed him king over them (1 Chronicles 11:1-3), and the meeting at Shechem expects something similar.

decisions.choice: the town of Shechem; their king
decisions.reason: Readable says that Shechem is a town and makes clear whose king Rehoboam was to be, as in 1 Kings 12:1.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן־נְבָט֙ וְה֣וּא בְמִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֔ח מִפְּנֵ֖י שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיָּ֥שָׁב יָרָבְעָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard Jeroboam son of Nebat, and he [was] in Egypt, where he had fled from [the] face of Solomon the king, and returned Jeroboam from Egypt.

en.L: And it happened, when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard [it] (and he [was] in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king), that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
en.B: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about it, he was in Egypt, where he had taken refuge from King Solomon, and he returned from Egypt.
en.R: Jeroboam son of Nebat was in Egypt. He had run away there from King Solomon. When he heard the news, he came back from Egypt.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam returned from Egypt, where 1 Kings 12:2 has "stayed in Egypt"
alternatives: and Jeroboam stayed in Egypt (1 Kings 12:2)
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 12:2 reads "and Jeroboam stayed (or lived) in Egypt". Chronicles reads "and Jeroboam returned from Egypt". The two verbs are written with the same letters and differ only in their vowels, and Chronicles adds "from", so here the sense "returned" is certain. The note at 1 Kings 12:2 discusses the two readings. Chronicles also lacks the word "still" ("he was still in Egypt"). Its account runs straight on: Jeroboam comes back, and the tribes call him to the meeting (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Jeroboam had fled to Egypt from Solomon
decisions.reason: Jeroboam, one of Solomon's officials, was told by the prophet Ahijah that he would rule ten tribes; Solomon tried to kill him, and he fled to Shishak king of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died (1 Kings 11:26-40). Chronicles does not tell that story but expects the reader to know it (9:29).

decisions.choice: heard [it]: news of Solomon's death and the meeting at Shechem
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. What Jeroboam heard is clear from what comes before: Solomon had died and Rehoboam had become king (9:31), and Israel was gathering at Shechem (verse 1).

decisions.choice: parentheses round the clause about Egypt
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 12:2, Literal marks off the background clause in the middle of the sentence, so that the main line, "when Jeroboam heard ... Jeroboam returned from Egypt", can be followed.

decisions.choice: the background first
decisions.reason: Readable says first where Jeroboam was and why, then what he did when he heard the news.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ וַיִּקְרְאוּ־ל֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥א יָרָבְעָ֖ם וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sent and called for him, and came Jeroboam and all Israel and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

en.L: And they sent and called him, and Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
en.B: So they sent and summoned him, and Jeroboam and all Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
en.R: So the people sent for him. Then Jeroboam and all the people of Israel came and said to Rehoboam,

decisions.choice: all Israel, where 1 Kings 12:3 has "all the assembly of Israel"
decisions.reason: Chronicles says "all Israel" where Kings says "all the assembly of Israel", and its verb "came" is written in the singular, so the note on the written and read forms in 1 Kings 12:3 does not arise here. Chronicles also has no parallel to 1 Kings 12:20, which tells of Jeroboam's return after the meeting; here he has already returned (verse 2), and he leads the people from the start.

decisions.choice: they sent: the tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it is the people of Israel gathered at Shechem (verse 1), who call Jeroboam to speak for them.

decisions.choice: came: singular, agreeing with Jeroboam
decisions.reason: The verb agrees with Jeroboam, named first; all Israel comes with him. The meaning is that they came together.

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "all the people of Israel" for "all Israel", as in verse 1.

source.text: אָבִ֖יךָ הִקְשָׁ֣ה אֶת־עֻלֵּ֑נוּ וְעַתָּ֡ה הָקֵל֩ מֵעֲבֹדַ֨ת אָבִ֜יךָ הַקָּשָׁ֗ה וּמֵעֻלּ֧וֹ הַכָּבֵ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ וְנַֽעַבְדֶֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your father made hard our yoke; and now lighten from [the] service of your father the hard and from his yoke the heavy which he put on us, and we will serve you.

en.L: "Your father made our yoke hard. And now lighten [some] of the hard service of your father and of his heavy yoke that he put on us, and we will serve you."
en.B: "Your father made our yoke hard. Now ease the harsh labor your father demanded and the heavy yoke he laid on us, and we will serve you."
en.R: "Your father made life hard for us. He put a heavy load on us, like a heavy yoke on an ox. Now make our hard work easier and our load lighter, and we will serve you."

decisions.choice: and now, where 1 Kings 12:4 has "and you, now"
decisions.reason: Kings has the people turn to Rehoboam with "and you" before "now". Chronicles has only "and now". Otherwise the words are the same as 1 Kings 12:4.

decisions.choice: yoke: the burden of the king's demands
decisions.reason: A yoke is the wooden bar laid on the necks of oxen so that they can pull. Here it stands for what Solomon required of his people: work on his buildings and the food supplied for his court (1 Kings 5:2-8, 27-28; 9:15; 11:28).

decisions.choice: service: work owed to the king
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for work or service; with "hard" it recalls Israel's hard service in Egypt (Exodus 1:14; 6:9). The people describe Solomon's rule in the words used of Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: lighten some of: a request for relief, not for an end to all service
decisions.reason: The preposition "from" means "part of". The people ask the king to reduce the load, and they promise to serve him if he does. Their loyalty depends on his answer.

decisions.choice: like a heavy yoke on an ox
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the yoke once and then speaks of a load, as in 1 Kings 12:4.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ע֛וֹד שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הָעָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Yet three days, and return to me. And went the people.

en.L: And he said to them, "Yet three days, and [then] return to me." And the people went.
en.B: He said to them, "Come back to me in three days." So the people left.
en.R: Rehoboam told them, "Come back to me in three days." Then the people went away.

decisions.choice: no "Go away": 1 Kings 12:5 has "Go away for three days"
decisions.reason: Kings has Rehoboam say "Go" before "three days". Chronicles leaves it out; that the people are to leave and come back is plain from "return to me" and from the end of the verse.

decisions.choice: three days: until the third day
decisions.reason: The people come back "on the third day" (verse 12), so the three days are counted with the first and last included, as was usual.

decisions.choice: Rehoboam told them
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֞ץ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־הַזְּקֵנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ עֹֽמְדִ֗ים לִפְנֵי֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אָבִ֔יו בִּֽהְיֹת֥וֹ חַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר אֵ֚יךְ אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב לָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And consulted the king Rehoboam with the elders who had been standing before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, How you counsel to bring back to this people word?

en.L: And King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, "How do you counsel [me] to return a word to this people?"
en.B: King Rehoboam then consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. "What answer do you advise me to give this people?" he asked.
en.R: Then King Rehoboam asked for advice from the older men who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. He asked them, "How should I answer these people?"

decisions.choice: the same as 1 Kings 12:6
decisions.reason: The words are those of 1 Kings 12:6, with two small changes of preposition ("before", "to this people") that do not change the sense.

decisions.choice: the elders: older men who had been Solomon's advisers
decisions.reason: The word means older men. Here they are senior members of the court who had served Solomon, set against the young men who had grown up with Rehoboam (verse 8); they are not the elders of the tribes.

decisions.choice: stood before: served as attendants and advisers
decisions.reason: To stand before a king is to wait on him and be ready to serve him (9:7; 1 Kings 1:2).

decisions.choice: return a word: give an answer
decisions.reason: "Bring back a word" is the usual Hebrew way of saying "answer"; it returns in verse 9.

decisions.choice: older men
decisions.reason: Readable says "older men" so that readers do not think of the leaders of the tribes.

source.text: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר אִם־תִּֽהְיֶ֨ה לְט֜וֹב לְהָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וּרְצִיתָ֔ם וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם דְּבָרִ֣ים טוֹבִ֑ים וְהָי֥וּ לְךָ֛ עֲבָדִ֖ים כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they spoke to him, saying, If you will be for good to this people and be favorable to them and speak to them words good, then they will be to you servants all the days.

en.L: And they spoke to him, saying, "If you will be good to this people and be favorable to them, and speak good words to them, then they will be slaves to you all the days."
en.B: They answered him, "If you are kind to this people and show them favor, and speak kind words to them, they will always be your servants."
en.R: They told him, "If you are kind to these people and treat them well, and if you speak kindly to them, they will always be your servants."

decisions.choice: be good to this people and be favorable to them, where 1 Kings 12:7 has "be a servant to this people today and serve them"
decisions.reason: In Kings the elders play on one word: if the king will be a servant to the people today and serve them, they will be his servants for good. Chronicles gives the same advice in other words: "if you will be good to this people and be favorable to them". It also lacks "today" and "answer them". In both, the elders promise lasting loyalty in return for a gracious answer now.

decisions.choice: be favorable to them: show them goodwill and grant what they ask
decisions.reason: The verb means to take pleasure in someone or to accept them with favor, as the LORD accepts an offering or a person (Leviticus 1:4; Psalm 147:11). Here the king would show the people goodwill by granting their request. It may also be taken as "satisfy them" or "win them over"; the advice is the same.

decisions.choice: good words: a kind and favorable answer
decisions.reason: "Good words" are gracious words that grant what is asked. The phrase can also mean a promise of good terms.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets out for this word, Literal keeps "slave" and Balanced and Readable say "servant". The point is loyal service, not ownership.

decisions.choice: kind; show them favor (Balanced), treat them well (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Be for good to" means to treat kindly; Balanced and Readable use the plain English words.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצֻ֑הוּ וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֶת־הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּ֔וֹ הָעֹמְדִ֖ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he abandoned the counsel of the elders which they counseled him, and consulted with the young men who had grown up with him, the ones standing before him.

en.L: And he forsook the counsel of the elders that they had counseled him, and he took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, those standing before him.
en.B: But he rejected the advice the elders had given him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.
en.R: But Rehoboam did not follow the older men's advice. Instead he asked the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.

decisions.choice: the same as 1 Kings 12:8
decisions.reason: The words are those of 1 Kings 12:8, except that Kings has "who" before "the ones standing before him". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: forsook: set aside, rejected
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or abandon. Rehoboam does not merely disagree with the elders' advice; he throws it aside.

decisions.choice: the young men: Rehoboam's companions of his own age
decisions.reason: The word usually means children or boys. Rehoboam was forty-one when he became king (12:13), so these are not boys; calling them by this word may hint at their lack of judgment.

decisions.choice: standing before him: serving him
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, to stand before the king is to serve him. These young men now held places at Rehoboam's court.

decisions.choice: did not follow
decisions.reason: Readable puts "forsook" in plain words and names Rehoboam.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם מָ֚ה אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים וְנָשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּר֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הָקֵל֙ מִן־הָעֹ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אָבִ֖יךָ עָלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, What you counsel, and we will bring back word [to] this people who have spoken to me, saying, Lighten from the yoke which put your father on us?

en.L: And he said to them, "What do you counsel, that we may return a word to this people who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten [some] of the yoke that your father put on us'?"
en.B: He asked them, "What do you advise? How should we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"
en.R: He asked them, "What do you advise? How should we answer these people? They said to me, 'Make the load your father put on us lighter.'"

decisions.choice: word for word as 1 Kings 12:9
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is the same as 1 Kings 12:9, and the wording here is the same.

decisions.choice: we: Rehoboam counts the young men in with himself
decisions.reason: To the elders Rehoboam said "to answer" (verse 6); to the young men he says "that we may answer". He treats them as partners in the decision.

decisions.choice: the people's request is repeated in short
decisions.reason: Rehoboam sums up the request of verse 4 in a few words and leaves out the people's promise to serve him.

source.text: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אִתּ֗וֹ הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ כֹּֽה־תֹאמַ֡ר לָעָם֩ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבְּר֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ לֵאמֹ֗ר אָבִ֨יךָ֙ הִכְבִּ֣יד אֶת־עֻלֵּ֔נוּ וְאַתָּ֖ה הָקֵ֣ל מֵעָלֵ֑ינוּ כֹּ֚ה תֹּאמַ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם קָֽטָנִּ֥י עָבָ֖ה מִמָּתְנֵ֥י אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke with him the young men who had grown up with him, saying, Thus you will say to the people who spoke to you, saying, Your father made heavy our yoke, and you lighten [it] from on us; thus you will say to them, My little [finger] [is] thick more than [the] loins of my father.

en.L: And the young men who had grown up with him spoke with him, saying, "Thus you shall say to the people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you, lighten [it] from on us'; thus you shall say to them: 'My little [finger] is thicker than the loins of my father.
en.B: The young men who had grown up with him answered, "The people said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make it lighter for us.' Give them this answer: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
en.R: The young men who had grown up with him answered, "The people said to you, 'Your father put a heavy load on us. Make it lighter for us.' So tell them this: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist! I will be much harder on you than he was.

decisions.choice: small differences from 1 Kings 12:10
decisions.reason: Kings has "spoke to him", "this people" and "thus you shall speak to them"; Chronicles has "spoke with him", "the people" and "thus you shall say to them". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: my little finger is thicker than my father's loins: I will be far harsher than my father
decisions.reason: The boast compares the smallest part of the new king with the thickest part of the old one. Rehoboam's least effort will weigh more on them than Solomon's greatest.

decisions.choice: my little [finger]
decisions.reason: The word means "my little one" or "my smallness"; the word for finger is not written but is understood. It appears only here and in the parallel at 1 Kings 12:10.

decisions.choice: loins: the waist and hips
decisions.reason: The word names the middle of the body, where a belt is worn, the thickest part of a man.

decisions.choice: the young men tell Rehoboam twice what to say
decisions.reason: "Thus you shall say ... thus you shall say" frames the people's words and then the answer the young men put into his mouth, which runs on through verse 11.

decisions.choice: waist
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "waist", the ordinary word for this part of the body; Literal keeps "loins".

decisions.choice: I will be much harder on you than he was
decisions.reason: Readable adds a plain sentence that explains the boast. Verse 11 says the same in other words.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה אָבִי֙ הֶעְמִ֤יס עֲלֵיכֶם֙ עֹ֣ל כָּבֵ֔ד וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עַֽל־עֻלְּכֶ֑ם אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֖י בָּֽעֲקְרַבִּֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And now my father loaded on you a yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with the whips, and I with the scorpions.

en.L: And now, my father loaded a heavy yoke on you, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I [will discipline you] with scorpions.'"
en.B: So then: my father laid a heavy yoke on you, but I will make your yoke heavier still. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.'"
en.R: My father put a heavy load on you, but I will make it even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions, which hurt far more!'"

decisions.choice: but I with scorpions: the verb is not repeated
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 12:11 repeats the verb: "but I will discipline you with scorpions". Chronicles leaves it to be understood from the line before. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: scorpions: a far crueler punishment than whips
alternatives: a whip fitted with barbs or spikes
a picture of the scorpion's sting
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for the scorpion. It may name a kind of whip fitted with barbs or spikes that bit into the skin, or the scorpion's sting may simply be set against the whip as a picture of far worse pain. Either way the meaning is the same: Rehoboam will punish much more harshly than Solomon did. See the note at 1 Kings 12:11.

decisions.choice: disciplined: punished in order to correct
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a father correcting a son (Deuteronomy 8:5; Proverbs 19:18). Here it names the harsh treatment of forced laborers by those set over them.

decisions.choice: [will discipline you] (Literal); will punish you (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb understood from the line before is written out, in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: which hurt far more
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the picture of the scorpion means, so that the threat is clear without a note.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל־הָעָ֛ם אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שׁ֥וּבוּ אֵלַ֖י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jeroboam and all the people to Rehoboam on the day the third, as had spoken the king, saying, Return to me on the day the third.

en.L: And Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
en.B: On the third day Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam, as the king had told them: "Return to me on the third day."
en.R: On the third day Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam, just as the king had told them to do.

decisions.choice: the same as 1 Kings 12:12
decisions.reason: The words are those of 1 Kings 12:12. Here the verb "came" is simply written in the singular, agreeing with Jeroboam, named first, so the note on the written and read forms in Kings does not arise.

decisions.choice: on the third day: the time Rehoboam had set
decisions.reason: The repeated words stress that the people did exactly what the king asked (verse 5). They kept their part; the king's answer follows.

decisions.choice: the king's words are not repeated
decisions.reason: Readable says that the people did as they were told instead of quoting the king again.

source.text: וַיַּעֲנֵ֥ם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ קָשָׁ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲזֹב֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered them the king hard, and abandoned the king Rehoboam the counsel of the elders.

en.L: And the king answered them harshly, and King Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the elders.
en.B: The king gave them a harsh answer. King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders.
en.R: The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam did not follow the older men's advice.

decisions.choice: small differences from 1 Kings 12:13
decisions.reason: Kings has "answered the people" and ends "that they had counseled him"; Chronicles has "answered them", names "King Rehoboam" as the one who rejected the advice, and leaves out the last clause. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: harshly: the same word as the "hard" service of verse 4
decisions.reason: The people asked to be freed from "hard" service; the king answers them "hard". The repeated word shows that he meets their complaint with more of what they complained of.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כַּעֲצַ֤ת הַיְלָדִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַכְבִּיד֙ אֶֽת־עֻלְּכֶ֔ם וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עָלָ֑יו אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֖י בָּעֲקְרַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke to them according to [the] counsel of the young men, saying, I will make heavy your yoke, and I will add to it; my father disciplined you with the whips, and I with the scorpions.

en.L: And he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "I will make your yoke heavy, and I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I [will discipline you] with scorpions."
en.B: He spoke to them as the young men had advised: "I will make your yoke heavy, and I will add to its weight. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions."
en.R: He followed the young men's advice and said, "I will put a heavy load on you, and I will make it even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions, which hurt far more!"

decisions.choice: I will make your yoke heavy
alternatives: My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text followed here reads "I will make your yoke heavy". Some Hebrew manuscripts and old translations read "My father made your yoke heavy", as in 1 Kings 12:14 and as the young men's advice runs (verses 10-11); in Hebrew the two readings differ by a few letters. The text as it stands makes sense: Rehoboam announces a heavy yoke and more besides.

decisions.choice: other differences from 1 Kings 12:14
decisions.reason: Kings has "I will add to your yoke" and "but I will discipline you with scorpions"; Chronicles has "I will add to it" and "but I with scorpions", leaving the verb understood as in verse 11.

decisions.choice: scorpions: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, a far crueler punishment than whips.

decisions.choice: [will discipline you] (Literal); will punish you (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the verb understood from the line before is written out.

decisions.choice: which hurt far more
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי־הָיְתָ֤ה נְסִבָּה֙ מֵעִ֣ם הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְמַעַן֩ הָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ בְּיַד֙ אֲחִיָּ֣הוּ הַשִּֽׁלוֹנִ֔י אֶל־יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־נְבָֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: And not listened the king to the people, for it was a turn of affairs from with God, in order to establish Yahweh his word which he spoke by [the] hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

en.L: And the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn [of events] from God, in order that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} might establish {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
en.B: So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events came from God, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} might fulfill the word {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.
en.R: So the king did not listen to the people. This was God's doing. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was making {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word come true, the message {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah, the prophet from Shiloh.

decisions.choice: from God, where 1 Kings 12:15 has "from the LORD"
decisions.reason: Kings says the turn of events was "from the LORD" and that the word was one "the LORD had spoken". Chronicles says it was "from God" and makes the LORD the one who establishes his word. Both say that the outcome came from the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: a turn of events: something brought about
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to turn" and means an outcome caused by someone. Kings uses a shorter form from the same root (1 Kings 12:15); this form appears only here. The Hebrew says it came "from with God": he brought it about.

decisions.choice: Rehoboam's own choice serves the LORD's purpose
decisions.reason: Rehoboam chose his answer himself (verses 8 and 13), yet the writer says the outcome came from God. The LORD had announced through Ahijah that he would tear ten tribes from Solomon's son because of Solomon's idolatry (1 Kings 11:11-13, 31-36). Chronicles does not tell that prophecy but names the prophecy of Ahijah as one of its sources (9:29).

decisions.choice: Ahijah the Shilonite: the prophet from Shiloh
decisions.reason: Ahijah came from Shiloh, where the tabernacle once stood (1 Samuel 1:3). He tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam as a sign (1 Kings 11:29-39). Here his name is spelled in its longer Hebrew form; it is the same man.

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: God's word comes "by the hand of" a prophet when the prophet speaks it for him.

decisions.choice: the prophet from Shiloh
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the Shilonite" and says that Ahijah was a prophet (9:29).

source.text: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹא־שָׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ לָהֶם֒ וַיָּשִׁ֣יבוּ הָעָ֣ם אֶת־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ׀לֵאמֹ֡ר מַה־לָּנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק בְּדָוִ֜יד וְלֹֽא־נַחֲלָ֣ה בְּבֶן־יִשַׁ֗י אִ֤ישׁ לְאֹהָלֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַתָּ֕ה רְאֵ֥ה בֵיתְךָ֖ דָּוִ֑יד וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And all Israel, that not listened the king to them, and brought back the people the king, saying, What [is] to us portion in David? And not inheritance in [the] son of Jesse! Each to your tents, Israel! Now see your house, David! And went all Israel to his tents.

en.L: And all Israel [saw] that the king did not listen to them, and the people answered the king, saying, \q "What portion [is there] for us in David? \q And no inheritance in the son of Jesse! \q Each man to your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David!" \q And all Israel went to its tents.
en.B: When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, the people answered the king: \q "What part do we have in David? \q We have no inheritance in Jesse's son! \q Each man to your tents, Israel! Now look after your own house, David!" \q So all Israel went home.
en.R: All Israel saw that the king would not listen to them. So they answered the king, \q "We have no share in David! \q We get nothing from Jesse's son! \q Everyone go home, Israel! David, look after your own family now!" \q So all the people of Israel went home.

decisions.choice: all Israel [saw]: the verb is understood
alternatives: the verb dropped out in copying
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here begins "And all Israel, that the king did not listen to them", without a verb. The verb "saw" of 1 Kings 12:16 is understood, and some Hebrew manuscripts and old translations have it.

decisions.choice: the cry of 1 Kings 12:16 and of Sheba's revolt (2 Samuel 20:1)
decisions.reason: The cry repeats 1 Kings 12:16, which echoes the cry of Sheba son of Bichri when he led Israel away from David (2 Samuel 20:1). Chronicles differs from Kings in small points: it lacks "saw" and "word" at the start, it has "each man" in "to your tents" as Sheba's cry does, and it ends "all Israel went".

decisions.choice: no portion, no inheritance: David's house is nothing to us
decisions.reason: A portion and an inheritance are a share in family land. The tribes say they have no stake in David's family and owe it nothing. Calling David "the son of Jesse" instead of by his name or title is a slight (1 Samuel 20:27; 2 Samuel 20:1).

decisions.choice: each man to your tents: go home
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Israel's days of living in tents. It breaks up the assembly: each man goes home, and the people refuse the king (2 Samuel 20:1; 2 Chronicles 7:10).

decisions.choice: see to your own house, David: let David's family rule its own tribe
decisions.reason: "House" means David's family and line of kings. The tribes tell the house of David to look after Judah, its own tribe, and leave the rest of Israel alone.

decisions.choice: the cry set in three lines
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 12:16, the people's answer is set as a short poem following the Hebrew divisions, with the last two calls sharing a line, and the narrative closing the verse stands as its own line. Literal and Balanced keep the wording of 1 Kings 12:16 and 2 Samuel 20:1 where the Hebrew is the same; "each man" follows 2 Samuel 20:1.

decisions.choice: We have no share; We get nothing; Everyone go home; family
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a plain statement and explains "to your tents" and "house", as in 1 Kings 12:16 and 2 Samuel 20:1.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִ֖ים בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם רְחַבְעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Israel, the ones dwelling in [the] cities of Judah, reigned over them Rehoboam.

en.L: But [as for] the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel who were living in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
en.B: But Rehoboam reigned over the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who lived in the towns of Judah.
en.R: But Rehoboam still ruled over the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who lived in the towns of Judah.

decisions.choice: word for word as 1 Kings 12:17
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is the same as 1 Kings 12:17, and the wording here is the same.

decisions.choice: the Israelites: here the people of all the tribes
decisions.reason: In this verse "Israelites" has its wide sense, the people descended from Jacob, and so includes the people of Judah and any from the northern tribes who had settled in Judah's towns. Chronicles often calls the people of Judah "Israel" (11:3; 12:1).

decisions.choice: but: set against the departure of Israel
decisions.reason: The sentence puts "the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah" first, to set them against the rest of Israel, who had just gone home (verse 16).

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers both cities and small walled towns. "Towns" fits most of the places in Judah.

decisions.choice: still
decisions.reason: Readable adds "still" to show that Judah stayed with Rehoboam while the rest went away.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־הֲדֹרָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַמַּ֔ס וַיִּרְגְּמוּ־ב֧וֹ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶ֖בֶן וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם הִתְאַמֵּץ֙ לַֽעֲל֣וֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֔ה לָנ֖וּס יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Rehoboam Hadoram, who [was] over the forced labor, and stoned him [the] sons of Israel [with] stone, and he died; and the king Rehoboam made himself strong to go up into the chariot to flee [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who [was] over the forced labor, and the sons of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And King Rehoboam made haste to go up into the chariot to flee [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: King Rehoboam then sent Hadoram, the officer over the forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to get up into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.
en.R: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram to the people. Hadoram was in charge of the men who were forced to work for the king. But the people of Israel threw stones at him until he died. King Rehoboam hurried to jump into his chariot, and he escaped to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Hadoram and "the sons of Israel", where 1 Kings 12:18 has Adoram and "all Israel"
decisions.reason: Kings names the officer Adoram and says that "all Israel" stoned him; Chronicles spells the name Hadoram and says "the sons of Israel". The rest of the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: Hadoram, over the forced labor
decisions.reason: The forced labor was the system of work gangs that built Solomon's temple, palace and cities (1 Kings 5:27-28; 9:15). Hadoram is the same man as Adoram in 1 Kings 12:18, and probably the same as Adoniram, who held this post under Solomon (1 Kings 4:6; 5:28); he is not the Hadoram son of the king of Hamath in 1 Chronicles 18:10. Sending the man in charge of the very burden the people complained of was a provocation, whatever Rehoboam meant by it.

decisions.choice: stoned him: put him to death as a group
decisions.reason: Stoning was a death carried out by a whole community. Here it shows that the people as a body rejected the king's authority.

decisions.choice: made haste: managed with effort
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong. Here it describes the king pulling himself together and getting into his chariot just in time; it was a narrow escape.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel (Literal); the Israelites (Balanced); the people of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The crowd that stoned Hadoram is named as the Hebrew names it, without a gender setting, since the verse speaks of an angry crowd and does not say who was in it.

decisions.choice: the men who were forced to work for the king
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "the forced labor" was.

decisions.choice: his chariot
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the chariot"; it was the king's own.

source.text: וַיִּפְשְׁע֤וּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּבֵ֣ית דָּוִ֔יד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And rebelled Israel against [the] house of David until the day the this.

en.L: So Israel has rebelled against the house of David to this day.
en.B: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
en.R: So Israel turned against the family of David, and it has stayed separate from it to this day.

decisions.choice: word for word as 1 Kings 12:19; no parallel to 1 Kings 12:20
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is the same as 1 Kings 12:19. Chronicles ends its account here. It has nothing like 1 Kings 12:20, where Israel makes Jeroboam king over all Israel, and it goes on with Rehoboam in Judah (11:1).

decisions.choice: Israel: here the northern tribes that broke away
decisions.reason: From this point "Israel" can name the kingdom of the northern tribes, and "Judah" the kingdom ruled by David's line from Jerusalem. Chronicles follows Judah and still uses "Israel" in its wider sense too, for the whole people of God, including those in Judah (11:3; 12:1).

decisions.choice: rebelled: broke away from its ruler
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a people throwing off the rule of its overlord, as Moab and Edom later rebelled against Israel and Judah (2 Kings 1:1; 2 Chronicles 21:8). It describes a political break, not only a quarrel.

decisions.choice: to this day: the words of the earlier account
alternatives: the day of the writer of Chronicles
decisions.reason: As at 5:9 and 8:8, the words come from the earlier account (1 Kings 12:19). By the time Chronicles was written the northern kingdom had long since fallen (2 Kings 17:6), so "this day" is the day of that account, though the north never returned to the house of David.

decisions.choice: the house of David: the royal line promised to David
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised David a lasting house, a line of kings (1 Chronicles 17:10-14). The split leaves that line ruling Judah only.

decisions.choice: Israel and Judah at every level
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 12, the names are kept as the Hebrew has them at every level, without "the northern kingdom" or "the southern kingdom"; the meaning decision explains them. Readable says "turned against ... stayed separate" for the lasting state the Hebrew verb describes.
